doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Playing dances, Purdue and the Paul Reegy band, summer at Sylvania, Ohio
summary: Pete rides to dances with a Mishawaka combo, is recruited to Purdue at 14, lives with the band members, and plays a summer quarry job with visiting name bands.

bands.name: Jimmy Bach and his Eight Cylinders in Music

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Were you anxious to get out of high school and get on with it?
Yes, really. I remember in fact I went to Purdue, there was a guy by the name of Paul Reegy was one of the youngest men, in engineering, in the faculty at Purdue, I think he

was 27, and he was on the faculty. And he played piano. And he was into logarithms and all that. Figuratively speaking, you know, he had a college band. And first of all I used to ride my bicycle up to the high school, which was about a mile away on Lincoln Way, which is the big main drag from Mishawaka, every Friday we used to play for dances. And I played all the jazz. And I remember having my tux and rolling up my pants so it wouldn’t get caught in the chain, and my trumpet, and getting down there I’d get off study hall early so I could make the 4:00 downbeat.

And I played with all these — we had two ladies also, saxophonists, and it was called Jimmy Bach and his Eight Cylinders in Music. And that was a big deal. And they went on to Purdue, engineering. And while they were up there a couple of years I think they had a New Years Eve gig and they needed another trumpet player, a ride man, and they said well you ought to get Pete Candoli, he does all the things with Cylinders. So they said well could you get him? One of those. So one of the guys came back, drove back from Mishawaka, which was 80 miles from Purdue, the campus, and drove me up there and I stayed all night and it was a big deal, I think I was 14.
And you’re the ride man, right? You’re the hot player.

Yeah, I had such a great time really, it was just marvelous. And then of course they became my guardians and got permission from my folks. Like I lived with them, I was 15 and I graduated at 16, but I went right on and stayed there at Purdue because Paul Reegy had the orchestra, and so I remember the second year we had a gig for the whole summer at Sylvania, Ohio, right below Toledo, at a big open quarry. And the band was going to be there all summer and I think they were bringing in name bands every other week for a couple of nights a week. Like Charlie Spivak came through and Sonny Dunham came through one night, and Carlos Gastel was their manager. He was a big heavy guy who had Peggy Lee and Nat King Cole, and he was managing Sonny Dunham. And of course I got to pick up on all these bands at that time. I think we were getting eight dollars for the week, and a place to stay and a meal ticket at the local restaurant. And this was—
